Theme

Town, shops & places · Conversation, family & daily routines

how can I help you? phrase

also can I help you?, what can I do for you?, may I help you?, how may I help you?

modern

Traupman 113

Quōmodo tibi ministrāre possum?

how can I help you? (a shop assistant to a customer)

Ministrāre is classically to wait on someone, above all at table (quō commodius tibi ministrētur, Cic. Fam. 16.14.2, Lewis & Short); the shop greeting is Traupman’s. Every word is classical; we have found no classical instance of the phrase.

Other words

  • Quōmodo possum tē juvāre? — how can I help you?

    also used · modern · Traupman 128

    Traupman’s words. Adjuvāre is as good, and the usual verb for helping someone in a task (see I’ll help you). Every word is classical; we have found no classical instance of the phrase.

See also I’ll help you, serve, shop assistant.
